findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed TCS foods not being cold held below 41 F in a broken prep cooler. CORRECTED: PIC and staff discarded TCS food items that were inside the prep cooler if they were prepared longer than 4 hours ago, and TCS items prepared under 4 hours were moved to a working cooler. This cooler cannot be used for service unless it is repaired (see Violation #33) or a Time as Control Policy is created and used. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at temperatures of 41 F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed that the prep cooler on the far end of the kitchen by the office was still observed not keeping the appropriate temperature range. The average temperature within the cooler using the infrared thermometer was 55F. Temperatures obtained by probing was 45F. PICs previously told Inspector that the unit will be repaired accordingly, but per PICs they are still waiting on a part. Cease using the prep cooler for cold holding until it is repaired. Ensure that the necessary repairs are done enabling the unit to have the appropriate temperature capacity.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was provided and the behavior was corrected.  Ensure that employees are reminded to always properly wash their hands before donning gloves in between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple items to be held past their seven day date mark (gyro meat- 10/31, salsa ranch- 10/27, and chipotle BBQ-10/27). CORRECTED- the gyro meat was discarded, and the PIC stated the other sauces had been remade since the sticker date, and the items were re-stickered with the correct dates. Ensure all Time/Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) food items are marked with the date they are prepared, and are used or discarded within seven days. The day of preparation or thawing counts as day one. To help ensure this practice takes place, ensure sauces are placed into a new container that has been clean and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The PIC stated their Allergen Awareness Certificate had expired, and they were unable to produce Allergen Awareness certificates for any Certified Food Protection Managers (CFM/CFPM). Inspector provided Allergen Awareness literature to the PIC, which included a web address to ANSI-accredited institutes. Ensure all CFMs obtain an Allergen Awareness certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed

 Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed

Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.

Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes or sanitizer are used to wipe stems between temperature checks, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portions of eggroll sauce were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 70F-75F on the prep table across from the salad cooler. Portions of salsa and sour cream in the same area were also at 70F. Portions were discarded. 
--Pitchers of dressings were out on the prep table across from the salad cooler. Ranch and blue cheese dressings were observed with internal temperatures of 57F and 76F respectively. All pitchers of dressing that were out in the salad area were discarded. A time control policy was established for working supplies of dressings/sauces held at room temperature during lunch and dinner service. 
--Working supply of lettuce stored in a stock pot on ice had surface temperatures at 46F-51F and internal temperatures of 46F-48F. Cold holding was discussed with emphasis on using a larger container for the ice bath to allow for submersion during storage. Portion of lettuce was placed in the walkin cooler for storage. 
--Pans containing portions of Italian beef, chicken wings, raw chicken strips, raw stuffed chicken, and eggrolls were held in a pan that was sitting within another pan containing ice. This is a new practice that started recently for storage of working supplies of these foods during lunch and dinner service. Internal temperatures were observed at 46F-59F depending on how much product was present and how foods were stocked in pans. All foods were placed out for service at 11:45am and were to be used or discarded by 5:45pm since foods were holding below 70F. A time control policy was established for these foods (see general comments). 
--TCS foods in the salad cooler were observed with temperatures at 52F-53F. Diced ham and turkey was checked in the top holding area and cottage cheese was checked in the bottom. Ice buildup was observed in the bottom of he unit (see #33). All TCS foods were discarded. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.citation_text:

Do not use the cooler for long term storage of TCS foods. Use time control for working supplies of foods during service (serve/discard within 4-6hrs based on temperature during use - see time control policy for details). 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:

Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness

Except for a plain ring such as a wedding band, while preparing food, food employees may not wear jewelry including medical information jewelry on their arms and hands.

findings.title: Allergen training as required

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 The stem of one food thermometer was observed with stuck on food debris. Thermometer was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. Proper use and maintenance of thermometers were discussed. Food thermometers need to be cleaned after use and prior to storage.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:

These foods were located in the middle section of the cooler and included salad greens, chicken skewers, pork, and blue cheese portions. Other foods in the bottom of the cooler on the far ends had internal temperatures at 43F, and foods in the top were at 40F-41F. TCS foods above 43F were discarded.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged fish portions were in the process of thawing in the walkin cooler at the time of inspection. Directions on the packaging states to remove vacuum packaging before thawing. At least one portion was fully thawed while others were still frozen. Management was advised to make sure the packaging removed prior to thawing. 
Frozen fish that are vacuum packaged (reduced oxygen packaging=ROP) and bear a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use need to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (packaging) either prior to thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, thawing by other means (e.g. under running water).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.
Equipment components such as doors, seals, and hinges shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

findings.citation_text:

Employee was advised on handwashing between handling the soiled and cleaned dishes and to also cease the practice of wiping hands on cloth towels. Soiled wiping cloth was placed in laundry bag, and the employee washed his hands prior to continuing dish washing tasks. 
Food employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Open gallon of milk in the walkin cooler had use by date of 4/17 and no date mark. The gallon of milk in question was discarded. Another open gallon of milk used to make chocolate milk with syrup in house was not labeled but was not past the product use by date. Person in charge provided a proper date mark for the chocolate milk.  
Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled

4-903.11 Caddies used for storage of clean utensils in the dish area were soiled with food crumbs. Clean the storage caddies daily/as needed, and maintain them clean to protect clean utensils from potential contamination.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

Nonfood-contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Foods in the salad cooler were observed with internal temperatures of 49°F-50°F. The cooler was observed to be holding around 50°F (see #4 below). All foods held in the bottom of the cooler overnight (pasta, cottage cheese, leafy greens, etc.) were discarded. Foods requiring time/temperature control for safety (TCS) in the top of the cooler were discarded and switched out with fresh product (tomatoes, cheese, boiled eggs, diced deli meat). Foods in the top were switched out around 3p; as long as products did not get above 70°F staff were advised they could serve or discard by 9p. Time control will be used for working supplies in the cooler until the cooler is able to maintain foods at 41°F/below.

Cold TCS food shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display, and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Two containers of cheese sauce in the freezer were labeled with dates and times of 12/17 and 10a. Internal temperatures for cheese sauce were 104°F and 80°F. Cheese sauce was well past the first 2hrs to get below 70°F and was not cooling properly. Both portions were reheated to 165°F to restart the cooling process.

Also, diced cooked chicken also prepared today around 10a had an internal temperature of 55°F. Plastic wrap was partially removed and product was placed in the freezer to finish rapidly dropping the temperature below 41°F.

Cooked TCS foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to monitor temperatures and verify foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling.
**Educational handouts were provided**

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Salad cooler was observed holding at 50°F during the inspection. Ice buildup was observed on the condenser fan in the bottom of the cooler. A call for service was made, and a technician arrived to service the salad cooler during the inspection. A tube was plugged and causing issue with freezing. Repairs were made during the inspection. Cooler may be used for long term cold storage when it is once again holding foods at 41°F/below.

All refrigeration units used to store TCS foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F/below.
(see general comments)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:

Proper locations for future use of fly strips were discussed (e.g. corners behind swinging doors, over dirty dish area, under sinks).

Food and equipment shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:

Properly store and protect foods at all times. Store food at least 6 inches off the floor.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750. 280  Soufflé cup was observed as a scoop in a container of cottage cheese. Soufflé cup was discarded. 

Use suitable utensils, such as scoops with handles, to avoid unnecessary manual contact with food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).

Bartender was observed wiping hands on a cloth towel at one point during the inspection. About three towels were observed on the back bar counter. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided

750.830g - Chlorine test kit was not available for checking sanitizer concentration at the dish machine. Chlorine test kit was purchased during the inspection and provided for use.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly

Cease the practice of dumping mop water in the storm sewer, and do not dispose of it anywhere other than a sanitary sewer connection.

Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Jacket was observed hanging on dry storage shelving. Jacket was removed from the shelving.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding

Portions of items left in the top overnight had internal temperatures at 43°F (cheese shreds) and 44°F (lettuce; sliced tomatoes). Time control will be used for all products in both the top and the bottom of the cooler during hours of operation. The cooler was just serviced recently; a part had to be ordered (see general comments for details).

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:

Handsinks are to be accessible at all times and stocked with soap and paper towels to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated

Store the cleaned and sanitized ice wand on a clean surface between uses, preferably on a clean baking sheet on the top shelf.

Food and equipment shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).

750.510 - One of the cooks was observed washing hands without proper technique. Faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to drying hands. Proper technique was discussed, and the employee was observed using proper technique for the remainder of the inspection.

Dry hands with a paper towel and then use the paper towel as a barrier to shut off the faucet.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - A damp wiping cloth was observed sitting out on the prep cooler at the cook line. Cloth was placed in the soiled linen storage bag.

Two of the sani-buckets in the kitchen were at 0-100ppm quat, and one of the dining area sani-buckets was less than 100ppm quat. All solutions were remade at proper concentration of 200ppm 

Maintain quat solutions at 150-400ppm as directed on label instructions. Frequent use of wiping cloths will wear down the chemical at an accelerated rate. Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours more frequently depending on use as solutions and wiping cloths become soiled.
Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:

Cook in charge of reheat process stated he began reheating the pork around 7a, and the product was ~100°F when placed in the counter top hot holding unit. Temperature was checked by inspector at ~1010a. Food was beyond the 2hr time frame for rapid reheat. Pork was discarded, and a new bag was retrieved to heat for service. 

Foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be reheated rapidly to 165°F or higher throughout the product. Reheat process should be completed within 2hrs or less. Properly reheat food to 165°F or above.
NOTE: Use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to verify foods are reheated to 165°F/above within 2hrs.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Foods in the walkin cooler were observed with prep dates of 4/28 and no time indicated to know when cooling process began. Portions of cooked noodles had surface and internal temperatures of 50F-60F and 60F-66F respectively. Portions of cooked rice had surface and internal temperatures of 50F and 45F-49F respectively, and taco meat had surface and internal temperatures of 76F and 104F respectively. Cook on duty stated he was unsure as to the time of prep for the products in question. Taco meat was reheated above 170F and then spread out on a baking sheet in the walkin cooler to properly cool. Cooked potentially hazardous foods (TCS) shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Utilize ice baths, ice wands, and spread foods out on baking sheets in the walkin freezer and cooler (stirring products frequently) to help rapidly cool foods. Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to ensure foods reach benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling.
Educational handout on quick chill methods was provided.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled

The noodles were portioned and allowed to be returned in the small batches into the walk-in cooler for cooling. Indicate the time on cooling foods. Monitor the cooling process. Use baking sheets (as you do for the rice) to cool dense starches. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours. ALSO, there is a deep pan of cheese sauce cooling in the walk-in cooler. The pan was covered, without a time, and a hot center of 115F. Use shallow, uncovered pans and indicate the time. Use an ice wand or ice bath as needed. An ice bath was present beneath the cheese sauce, however, the container holding the ice bath is the same size container observed holding cheese sauce.
